note: Reviewed npm advisories that do NOT gate the build, each with the reason it
does not reach this app. Anything npm audit reports and this file does not
list fails `npm run check:advisories`.
A dependency advisory is not automatically a vulnerability in the thing that
depends on it. It is a vulnerability in a code path, and the question is
whether this app can reach that path. 'We ship the package' is the start of
the answer, not the end of it -- but neither is 'probably fine'. An entry
here has to name the specific entry point and say what calls it, so the claim
is checkable by the next person instead of inherited on trust.
The bar for adding an entry: an upgrade is not available or breaks the app,
AND the vulnerable path is not reachable. Both halves, written down.
Entries expire. `reviewed` is the date someone last checked the reasoning
against the actual code; the check warns on any entry older than a year,
because 'unreachable' is a statement about a codebase that keeps changing.
The first entry this file ever held was wrong, and it is worth writing down
how. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6 in @xmldom/xmldom was accepted on 2026-09-02 on the
reasoning that no upgrade existed: mammoth pins ^0.8.6, and 0.9 made
parseFromString's mimeType argument mandatory, so overriding to 0.9.12 broke
the shipped .docx path in a real browser. All of that was true. The
conclusion was not -- 0.8.15 backported the fix inside mammoth's own range
and had been published on 2026-08-21, eleven minutes before the 0.9.12 that
got tested and twelve days before the entry was written. The upgrade was
there; only the 0.9 door was tried.
`npm audit --json` had been saying so the whole time, in the same payload the
check already parsed: `fixAvailable: true`. So the check now reads it. An
entry here for an advisory npm reports as fixable fails the run, whatever the
prose says -- 'an upgrade is not available' is half the bar for an entry, and
it was the half nothing checked.

why: No upgrade exists: the advisory covers every sprintf-js release through 1.1.3, the newest. npm's offered fix is mammoth 0.3.29 from 2015 in place of the installed 1.12.0 -- a downgrade of the Word-document reader, which check-advisories no longer counts as a fix.

Unreachable: sprintf-js arrives only as mammoth -> argparse@1.0.10 -> sprintf-js@1.0.3. Inside mammoth, argparse is required by bin/mammoth, its command-line tool, and by nothing under lib/ or browser/. The app reaches mammoth through `import("mammoth")` in src/readout/extractText.ts, which resolves lib/index.js with the browser field's substitutions, and the built bundle contains neither 'argparse' nor 'sprintf'. This repo never runs the mammoth CLI.

The flaw is unbounded precision specifiers in a format string, a denial of service. Even if it were reached, the format strings are argparse's own help templates, not anything a household's document supplies.
